answer: I would like to talk about the friend whose company I probably enjoy most. A person I always enjoy talking to is a close friend of mine who has a genuinely curious mind. We met at a book club at the local library about four years ago, and since then we have met for tea almost every week, usually at a small café near the river. Our conversations can start with something trivial and end up exploring philosophy, travel or politics, which I find endlessly [[stimulating]]. Last week, for instance, we started talking about a cricket match and somehow ended up debating whether ambition really makes people happy. What makes talking to him so enjoyable is that he actually listens, rather than just waiting for his turn to speak. He is also wonderfully [[open-minded]], so I can share half-formed thoughts without fear of being judged. I think good conversation is a bit of an art, and he is a master of it, although he would never admit that. He knows when to be serious and when to be [[playful]], which keeps things from ever feeling heavy. Honestly, I always come away from our chats feeling energised and having learned something new. In a world where so much communication happens through screens, having someone you can talk to for hours is genuinely [[precious]]. I never take those conversations for granted, and I think they have made me a far better listener and a slightly more thoughtful person as well.

followUps.q: Do you prefer talking face to face or online?
followUps.answer: Face to face, definitely. You can read someone's expressions and tone properly, and the conversation flows more naturally. Online chats are convenient, but they often feel rather [[stilted]] by comparison.
It depends on who I am with. With close friends and family I can talk for hours, but in large groups of strangers I tend to be quieter and listen more than I speak.

note: Added how I know him (a library book club, weekly tea), a concrete example of how our talks wander and a reflective close.
